question: How severe was the July 20 'Sansad Chalo' crackdown, and who bore the brunt of it?

sideA.label: CJP / Protesters
sideA.text: The CJP claimed roughly 150 protesters were hospitalized and about 70 detained, with hospital sources logging 60+ injured and 65+ medico-legal cases at Ram Manohar Lohia Hospital by 7 p.m.

sideB.label: Delhi Police
sideB.text: Delhi Police reported 118 of their own personnel injured, framing the operation as a proportionate response to an unauthorized march toward Parliament during the monsoon session.

resolution: Independently verified figures sit between the two accounts: RML Hospital documented 65+ medico-legal cases and Safdarjung confirmed at least one pellet-gun wound, but the CJP's higher hospitalization tally has not been independently corroborated.

question: Was a protester struck by a live bullet during the July 20 crackdown?

sideA.label: Protester's family / rights groups
sideA.text: Allege a protester suffered ear trauma consistent with a live-round graze during the security response.

sideB.label: Delhi Police
sideB.text: Attribute the injury to blunt-force trauma sustained during the crush of the crowd, not gunfire.

resolution: Unresolved as of Jul 25; both the Delhi High Court and Chief Justice Surya Kant's bench declined to review video evidence when petitioned.

question: Did Delhi Police use pellet guns against protesters on July 20?

sideA.label: Delhi Police (public statement)
sideA.text: Publicly denied using pellet guns against the crowd at Jantar Mantar.

sideB.label: Hospital records / protesters
sideB.text: Safdarjung Hospital confirmed treating at least one pellet-gun wound, and police general diary entries separately recorded two Rapid Action Force rounds fired.

resolution: Physical and medical evidence contradicts the police's initial public denial; no formal correction or disciplinary finding was reported.

question: Was the CJP-led protest movement backed by foreign funding?

sideA.label: PIL petitioner (Satish Kumar Aggarwal / Akhil Bharat Hindu Mahasabha)
sideA.text: Alleges the July 20 protest was part of a broader conspiracy involving foreign-funded organizations and seeks an NIA investigation plus transfer of related FIRs.

sideB.label: Ministry of External Affairs / CJP
sideB.text: The MEA said it had 'no information to share' supporting the claim; CJP spokesperson Ratna Singh called the allegation 'politically motivated.'

resolution: The Delhi High Court agreed to hear the PIL on Jul 24, but no NIA probe had been ordered by the time the government reached its Jul 25 settlement with protest leaders.

question: Did DCP Sandeep Lamba assault a female protester on camera?

sideA.label: Protesters / Saket Gokhale (activist)
sideA.text: Video footage circulated appearing to show DCP Lamba slapping a female protester; Gokhale filed a formal FIR complaint over the incident.

sideB.label: Delhi Police
sideB.text: No public statement confirming disciplinary action or disputing the footage was documented in press coverage through Jul 25.

resolution: Unresolved; footage was widely shared but no independent departmental inquiry outcome had been reported as of the protest's conclusion.

question: Was volunteer Mohammad Junaid unlawfully detained and threatened by police?

sideA.label: Mohammad Junaid / family
sideA.text: Says he was picked up by police in Delhi, held for six hours, threatened, and dropped off in Dehradun; family alleges subsequent harassment by UP Police.

sideB.label: Police (no on-record response found)
sideB.text: No confirmation or denial from Delhi Police or UP Police was located in press coverage.

resolution: Reported by multiple outlets covering the crackdown's aftermath; no independent inquiry outcome has been confirmed.

question: Were violent actors embedded among the protesters, justifying police surveillance?

sideA.label: Delhi Police
sideA.text: Say they identified 2,873 men with criminal antecedents — including convictions or charges for sexual assault, murder, and POCSO offences — present at protest sites between Jul 20–25.

sideB.label: CJP / student groups
sideB.text: Dismiss this as a pretext for surveillance and intimidation, pointing to a PIL alleging police photography and videography of protesters created an 'atmosphere of intimidation.'

resolution: Unresolved; neither the scale of the police claim nor the intimidation allegation has been independently audited.

question: How many NEET aspirants died by suicide during the leak-to-retest window?

sideA.label: CJP
sideA.text: Cited 11 confirmed suicides in the 46 days between the May 12 cancellation and the June 21 re-exam, demanding ₹1 crore compensation per family from the government.

sideB.label: Other press tallies
sideB.text: Some ground reporting placed the toll as high as 13, tracking additional cases not captured in the CJP's initial count.

resolution: No single official government count has been published; the Jul 25 settlement pledged 'maximum compensation per existing rules' without confirming a final death toll or per-family amount.

question: How many protesters were formally targeted for prosecution nationwide?

sideA.label: CJP
sideA.text: Claims 100+ arrests took place after Jul 25 despite the government's assurances, and cites Mumbai Police FIRs registered against roughly 400 people.

sideB.label: Government
sideB.text: Pledged on Jul 25 to withdraw police cases against non-violent protesters in NDA-ruled states and take no future punitive action.

resolution: No consolidated national arrest or FIR figure has been independently verified; the scope of the government's case-withdrawal commitment (limited to NDA-ruled states) leaves cases elsewhere unresolved.

question: How widespread were the CBSE On-Screen Marking (OSM) errors?

sideA.label: CBSE / Ministry of Education
sideA.text: Acknowledged roughly 5,000 blurred-sheet cases and 23 candidate-mismatch cases out of about 98 lakh answer sheets — a small fraction of the total, and cut revaluation fees in response.

sideB.label: Affected students and parents
sideB.text: Say the true error rate is much higher, citing widespread unexplained low marks in Physics, Chemistry and Mathematics among students who scored strongly on competitive exams like JEE Main.

resolution: The Ministry's fee reduction implicitly acknowledged the scale of complaints without conceding a higher official error count than the ~5,000 figure.

question: Should NEET be scrapped entirely or reformed?

sideA.label: DMK (Tamil Nadu) and allied opposition
sideA.text: Argue scrapping NEET is the only way to end recurring irregularities and student suicides linked to the exam.

sideB.label: Union Government
sideB.text: Chose to retain NEET while tightening security and penalties through the Public Examinations Amendment Act rather than abolishing the exam.

resolution: Unresolved nationally; the Centre proceeded with amendment legislation rather than abolition, leaving the scrap-vs-reform debate especially live in Tamil Nadu.

question: Was Dharmendra Pradhan personally at fault for the exam failures, or did he resign to protect students from prolonged conflict?

sideA.label: Opposition / protesters
sideA.text: Demanded Pradhan's resignation as the minister accountable for NTA and CBSE lapses under his watch.

sideB.label: Pradhan / BJP
sideB.text: His resignation letter framed the decision as taking 'moral responsibility' for developments while defending the government's overall crisis handling, without admitting personal wrongdoing.

resolution: Pradhan resigned Jul 25 without an explicit admission of personal fault, satisfying the protesters' central demand without conceding their underlying accountability narrative.

question: Was Sonam Wangchuk's hunger strike a politically partisan act against the BJP government?

sideA.label: Sonam Wangchuk
sideA.text: Stated the movement had 'no political colour' and represented an appeal for education accountability and reform, not partisan politics.

sideB.label: Government-aligned commentators
sideB.text: Some officials and commentators characterized the CJP-led movement as opposition-aligned, noting Congress and other opposition parties' vocal backing.

resolution: Unresolved; roughly 65 opposition MPs publicly pledged support to Wangchuk, complicating his 'non-political' framing even as he maintained the movement's demands were policy-focused.

question: Why was the UGC-NET June 2026 exam partially re-conducted in August?

sideA.label: NTA
sideA.text: Says an internal committee found content and procedural errors in the English, Commerce and Sociology papers after student complaints, prompting a re-conduct.

sideB.label: NSUI / Congress
sideB.text: Frame it as evidence the NTA remains structurally unreformed despite the NEET crisis and the new amendment act, and demand broader accountability.

resolution: The NTA ordered the three papers re-conducted on Aug 16; whether this reflects an isolated error or systemic dysfunction remains an open political question as of Aug 20.

question: Is the government's compensation pledge for suicide victims' families adequate?

sideA.label: CJP
sideA.text: Demanded ₹1 crore in compensation per family of the 11 identified suicide victims.

sideB.label: Government (Jul 25 pledge)
sideB.text: Agreed to pay 'maximum compensation... per existing rules' without committing to the ₹1 crore figure sought by protest leaders.

resolution: Exact compensation amounts per family had not been independently confirmed or published as of Aug 20.

question: How many NSUI protesters were detained or injured at the Aug 17 UGC-NET protest outside the NTA office?

sideA.label: NSUI
sideA.text: Says Delhi Police and CRPF personnel detained protesters after they attempted to breach barricades, and that several NSUI members were injured during the police action.

sideB.label: Delhi Police (no on-record figures found)
sideB.text: No official detention or injury count, or public statement on the police response, was located in press coverage.

resolution: Unresolved; multiple outlets confirmed detentions and clashes occurred, but no independently verified figures for injuries or detentions have been published.

question: Is a CBI probe needed into Jharkhand's JPSC/JSSC recruitment-exam irregularities, or is the state's own response sufficient?

sideA.label: JPSC-JSSC Reforms Manch / Devendra Nath Mahto
sideA.text: Says only a federal CBI investigation can credibly establish accountability for years of alleged paper leaks and TDPL malpractice, and has vowed a 'phase two' protest until one is ordered.

sideB.label: Government of Jharkhand
sideB.text: Points to an ongoing state CID probe (which has already made 20 arrests, including a former JPSC chairman), a new exam-reforms committee under IAS officer Amitabh Kaushal, and Supreme Court/High Court monitoring of the JSSC-CGL process as adequate accountability measures.

resolution: Unresolved as of Aug 24; the government cancelled the tainted exams but declined the CBI demand, while the Supreme Court has now issued notice to the Centre, Jharkhand government, JPSC and CBI on a separate Article 32 petition (Devgan v. Union of India) alleging exam rigging, with Chief Justice Surya Kant signaling skepticism of the state's internal probes.

question: Does the Jharkhand High Court's stay of the exam cancellations undo the protesters' main victory?

sideA.label: Protesters / JPSC-JSSC Reforms Manch
sideA.text: Argue the stay lets potentially tainted appointments stand pending a slow court process, undermining weeks of protest and the government's Aug 17 concession.

sideB.label: Petitioning candidates (already appointed)
sideB.text: Say they cleared the exams on merit and should not lose their jobs over irregularities attributed to a private vendor and other candidates, and argue due process was denied when the cancellations were issued without a hearing.

resolution: Unresolved; the High Court's interim order preserves the appointments pending investigation, with the next hearing set for Sep 15, 2026, and warns that anyone shown to have benefited from fraud will still lose their post.

question: Did police and ruling-party workers assault female protesters at the Aug 22 Gandhi Maidan demonstration?

sideA.label: JPSC-JSSC Reforms Forum / protesters
sideA.text: Say police and JMM workers used force including assaulting female demonstrators after marchers deviated from the approved route to burn CM Soren's effigy.

sideB.label: Ranchi City DCP K.V. Raman
sideB.text: Said police used only 'mild force' after protesters disregarded the route given by the administration, disputing the characterization of the police response.

resolution: Unresolved; no independent injury tally, video review, or departmental inquiry outcome has been published as of Aug 25.

question: Did BPSC exam controller Rajesh Kumar Singh compare protesting students to barking dogs?

sideA.label: Students / Opposition (Tejashwi Yadav)
sideA.text: Say Singh's 'Hathi chale bazaar, kutta bhaunke hazar' remark was a direct insult equating protesting aspirants with dogs, and demand a public apology.

sideB.label: Rajesh Kumar Singh
sideB.text: Says the proverb was 'twisted and presented out of context' on social media and that he had no intention of hurting the sentiments of any individual or group.

resolution: Unresolved; CM Samrat Choudhary ordered Singh's suspension on Aug 24 regardless of the disputed intent, treating the political fallout as sufficient grounds for action.

question: Is there concrete evidence of a paper leak in the 70th BPSC preliminary exam?

sideA.label: Protesting aspirants
sideA.text: Circulated videos and screenshots they say show leaked questions ahead of the exam, and demand the 70th BPSC prelims be cancelled and re-held.

sideB.label: Bihar Public Service Commission
sideB.text: Says it has found no concrete evidence of a leak in the videos and screenshots shared by aspirants and has declined to cancel the exam.

resolution: Unresolved as of Aug 27; the government's reform package addressed procedural transparency and the TRE-4 format but stopped short of cancelling the 70th BPSC exam or ordering an independent leak probe.
